Barzolvolimab was initially studied in chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) and chronic inducible urticaria (CIndU), diseases where mast cell degranulation plays a central role in the onset and progression of the disease. ● In September 2026 we announced positive topline results from two Phase 3 studies of barzolvolimab in CSU.
We plan to present EMBARQ-CSU data at an upcoming medical meeting and submit a BLA to the FDA in 2027. ● A Phase 2 study in CSU has been completed.

Based on results from completed Phase 1 and Phase 2 studies and the topline data from both ongoing Phase 3 trials in CSU (Q4W dosing), barzolvolimab has the potential to offer symptom free complete control (absence of itch and hives, UAS7=0) and clinically meaningful improvements in quality of life and angioedema in a majority of patients.

Secondary endpoints included safety and other assessments of clinical activity including ISS7 (weekly itch severity score), HSS7 (weekly hive severity score) and AAS7 (weekly angioedema activity score). 22 Table of Contents ​ Topline data from this study were presented in November 2023 and 12 week treatment results were presented at the AAAAI Annual Meeting in February 2024.

Prurigo Nodularis (PN) In July 2026, we announced topline results from a Phase 2 study in prurigo nodularis (PN), a chronic skin disease characterized by the development of hard, intensely itchy (pruritic) nodules on the skin.
Topline results demonstrated that the trial did not meet primary or key secondary endpoints at Week 12 at either dose level evaluated.
Topline data from the study is expected in late 2026.
